              HQ/S/113/Air                                      4 October 1979


              Lieutenant Colonel F.J. Markcrov
              1 Aviation Regiment
              OAKEY QLD 4401




                           I recently had the pleasure of operating in the Windorah
              district with two pilots from 173 Squadron, First Lieutenant•
              Laurie Scerescini and Gezwyn Evans.    In each case we operat d for
              four days for long hours and of ten under trying conditions.

                        I found both officers aost helpful, courteous and
              professional, both on and off duty, and a credit to the Army in all
              respects.   I would also like to thank Major Damien Aird for his help
              and unquestioning co-operation.

                        Dear Sir,
                                We ref er to your report to the RAAF of an unusual
                      aerial sighting on the evening of 9 April 1978 and, as you
                      may already be aware, wish to inform you that the object was
                      a meteorite entering the earth's atmosphere.    The meteorite
                      was reported by observers from as far north as Cooktown in
                      North Queensland and is believed to have splashed into the sea
                  •
                      somewhere off Newcastle in N.s.w ••
                                          Thank you for your interest.

             HQAMB 5/113/Air(35)                                    4 January 1978

             Mr D. Hahner
             63 Stafford Street
             BOOVAL QLD 4304

             Dear Sir,


                       With reference to your report of an unusual aerial sighting on
             2 January and our telephone conversation of 3 January 1978, further
             investigation has revealed that the most probable cause was the star Hamel,
             which had risen in the direction of your sighting.     The unusual effects
             described by you are not uncou1111on if unusual atmospheric conditions prevail
             at the time or it is viewed through pollution in the lower layers of the
             earth's atmosphere.   These conditions have given rise to many similar
             reports over a number of years.

                         We trust that this explanation is satisfactory.


                                                                     Yours faithfully,




                                                                                 -
                                                                      F.E. BURT!')
                                                                     'Wi!lg Co•u•uander
                                                                     for Officer Cou•

             HQAMB 5/113/Air(34)                                 4 January 1978


          Mr P. McKechnie, MLA
          2 Belwood Street
          STANTHORPE QLD 4380

          Dear Sir,

                    Your letter reporting an unusual aerial sighting made by
          Mr Matthew Vale bas been received at this Headquarters.   A report form,
          'Report of Unusual Aerial Sightings', has been sent to Mr Vale and on
          its completion and return to us an investigation will be conducted into
          the matter.


                                                                  Yours fait fully,



                                                                                 •

                                                                  (F:E. BURTT)
                                                                  Wing Commander
                                                                  for Officer Commanding

                      As very little information was contained in bis letter, could you

             are that it was either the plan t Jupit r or the bright atar Sirius.       It
             is not unusual for reports of t his nat ure to be prompted by apparent unusual
             behaviour of the brighter stars or planets.     Fl•1ct11ations in brightness,
             position or colour of a combination of these can be caused by at oapheric
             scintillation - varyiug atmospheric d nsity layers.      Upper at ospheric
             pollution can also produce qui t e r   rkable effects from time to time.
                       However, the most probable cause of the sighting is a man made
             object; a fragment from t he Pageoa sp ce vehicle which was la nched in 1966.
             This particular piece of space d bris (there are presently 4141   n-made
             objects ranging from satellites nd sp ce-labs to rocket casings and
             frasments) is listed as one of the more brightly luminous objects and was
             in the position of your sight ing on 2 y 1977.
                           Trusting this explanation is satisfactory.
